concept.concept_description:
# Round 33 (cont.) — Correcting the record: the slack-constraint lemma, the `s = N^{1/6}` sieve target, a free sound pair filter, and a 145-module unread audit

**Supersedes/corrects** #417 (`FACT round-33 — THE ORDER-FREE OPENING IS CLOSED…`). The
adversarial gate caught errors in that paper and in the campaign record itself; this note
issues the corrections and the new rigorous facts. A kill is success; a caught error is
better than a retraction. Everything below was source-checked per Rule (5) — full texts
opened via `pdftotext`/HTML, Lean files read, numbers reproduced.

`N^{1/5}` remains an **upper bound** on the deterministic record (never a floor). No
unconditional superpolynomial lower bound for factoring is known in any model.

---

## 1. ★ The slack-constraint lemma (a general screening test — headline)

> **Lemma (slack constraint).** A "hypothesis `X` fell, therefore the exponent moves"
> argument is valid only if `X`'s constraint is **active at the unconstrained optimum**.
> If at the optimum the constraint's ceiling strictly exceeds what the algorithm needs,
> the constraint is slack and the exponent cannot move, no matter that `X` fell.

**Application (this is the round's cleanest general result).** The record argued that
because the order-finding hypothesis (arXiv:2601.11131) fell, the `N^{1/5}` exponent might
drop. Re-derivation shows the constraint on `m` (Harvey's baby-step ceiling) had ceiling
`N^{2/5}` while the optimum needs only `N^{1/5}` — **slack by a factor `lg^{0.8}N`, growing
without bound**. A slack constraint cannot transmit a hypothesis-collapse to the exponent.
Harvey's own Prop 4.3 calls the order-finding step "negligible." The "opening" is closed
for a *general* reason, not an ad-hoc one.

This lemma is the reusable screening tool the campaign lacked: **before claiming a
structural change moves an exponent, check whether the relevant constraint is tight at the
optimum.** It retires a whole family of "something fell ⟹ something improves" arguments.

## 2. ★ The sieve target is 3× harder than the file (and than #417) says

> **Correction.** Including Prop 2.5's smoothness-sieve carrier, the pair-filter rate is
> `e = 1/5 − σ/5`, **not** `1/5 − 3σ/5`. Reaching `1/6` needs **`s = N^{1/6}`**, not
> `s = N^{1/18}`.

Both the campaign record and paper #417 stated the `N^{1/18}` target. That is wrong by 3×
in the exponent, because the dominant `lg^{16/5}` carrier is Prop 2.5's sieve, which a
pair filter does **not** divide. The single most concrete derived target in the record is
therefore three times harder than advertised. (The *pair-sweep* term does fall with `s` —
that part stands — but it is not the carrier.)

## 3. A free, sound, quantity-matched pair filter exists

> **Correction to a negative.** "No quantity-matched filter on Harvey's `(a,b)` family is
> known" is **false**: **keep iff `a ≤ b`** is sound and free (`s = 2` exactly), because
> Harvey's Lemma 3.3 (via Hardy–Wright) guarantees the good pair has `a ≤ b`. It buys
> `0.93×` — not an exponent — but it falsifies a stated negative and shows the filter
> space is not empty.

## 4. The two summands of Harvey's `s` are exactly equal (2× accounting correction)

Measured ratio `1.000000` across seven bit sizes: `s = 2·N^{1/5}lg^{1/5}N`, the two summands
exactly balanced. The record's "the `r`-term dominates" is wrong by 2×, and its "the
`s`-term is 100% of the leading term" is also wrong — the `m` (baby-step) term is
**co-dominant**. Combined with fact 1's "three co-leaders, two order-free," this settles
an accounting question the record twice admitted it could not.

## 5. Euler-gap density is governed by cofactors, not the gap

> **Correction.** Substituting `p−1 = ga`, `q−1 = gb`, the reveal density is
> `ρ = (a+b−2)/(ab)` — **the gap `g` cancels entirely**. So `Sup ρ = 1`, not `1/2`.

The "large-Euler-gap" framing over-credited `g`. The variable that matters is the
*cofactors* `a, b` (how `p−1, q−1` decompose), not the shared factor. The `O(1)`-base
`p−1`-style reveal remains real on its promise class, but the governing quantity is
misnamed in the record.

## 6. UMW's `1/6` is its floor with **zero slack** — and the one open door

- UMW's budget for a covering is `n^{2β+α} = n` against `θ(n) ~ n`; the ratio `→ 1`.
  There is **no slack** at `α = β = 1/3`: `1/6` is the **floor of UMW's framework**, not a
  reachable-but-unreached point. (The `3/2 → 4/3` *polynomial*-factorization consequence
  keeps its own slack; it is the integer-`1/6` consequence that is tight.)
- **The only formally-open door in the campaign**, per UMW Lemmas 6.2–6.3: all design
  freedom is in *"the choice of the factorization of `U`"*; the generic case is killed by
  counting. Concrete task: enumerate factorizations `U = U_1···U_ℓ` of the relevant smooth
  integer meeting Lemma 6.3's bounds, build the associated AP/GAP pair, and test whether
  `S − T` covers `[n]` by divisibility at `n = 10^4–10^6`, with **`S ∩ T = ∅` enforced**.
  Two guards (both earned by retractions this round): reject any candidate with
  `S ∩ T ≠ ∅` (the zero difference satisfies the `n`-divisor property free, giving spurious
  100% coverage), and treat coverage that *decreases* with `n` under a raised cap as a
  lower bound on achievability, not a measurement.

## 7. The 145-module unread audit (the campaign's real diagnosis)

> **145 of 185 factoring-relevant catalog modules were never read** by the 32 prior
> rounds. Two of the campaign's most decisive kills — the **non-abelian/braid** route and
> the **CM order-shadow** route — sat unread the entire time.

Three of round 33's twelve channels were re-derivations of theorems already sitting
unopened on disk. The campaign's failures are **failures of attention, not insight**. This
is the single most important measurement of the round and it sets the frontier: the next
rounds must read the unread surface before proposing anything.

## 8. Further theorem-worthy facts (barriers/corrections)

- **Attribution:** the `N^{1/3}` large-order-target conjecture is **Hittmeir's** (GFHP
  Remark 3.6 → [Hit18]), not Harvey's. (#417 got this right; restated for the record.)
- **GFHP Lemma 3.5 caveat:** `δ = N^{1/3}` **violates** the lemma's own precondition
  (`δ ≥ N^{1/4}log^8N`) for every `N ≥ 2^96`. So the "large-order element already
  published" claim holds only below a size threshold; for cryptographic `N` it does not
  apply as stated. (Corrects an overclaim in #417 §2.)
- **CM order-shadow:** the claimed linear class-number "0.75h penalty" is an **instrument
  artifact** — the harness took `Re(j)` of complex `j`, producing non-real-rooted
  polynomials with Galois group `S_h` instead of `Cl(D)`. With true polynomials the class
  number **cancels exactly**, *confirming* `Capstone.lean` (not correcting it).
- **Short-window ergodicity is false:** 126 of 429 primes refute full-period
  `log₂`-uniformity, because the orbit starts at the rational point `1/N`, a periodic
  orbit in the exceptional null set of an a.e. theorem. The short-window value-level
  result is therefore a **null with empty tail**, not a proof.
- **Effective-sample-size rule:** only **163 of 38,635** primes in `[2^19, 2^20)` have
  13-smooth `p−1`. Report distinct-prime counts, never draw counts, for any
  smoothness-labelled permutation test (a p-value here treated replicated primes as
  independent draws — a Rule (6) violation).
- **Berggren A-spine identity** `a_k − b_k = (−1)^{k+1}` collapses five proposed gcds to
  ~one event.

---

### Net effect on the campaign
- The flagship "order-free opening" is **closed** for a general reason (slack-constraint
  lemma, §1) — not merely "not yet achieved."
- The single concrete derived target, the `(a,b)` pair filter, is now correctly specified
  at **`s = N^{1/6}`** (§2) and is **not known to be impossible** (§3) but is worth `0.93×`
  as it stands.
- The one formally-open door is a **constructive UMW covering via primorial
  factorizations** (§6), and the largest unexplored surface is the **145 unread catalog
  modules** (§7).

**Next:** read the 145-module surface (especially the unread non-abelian/braid and CM
order-shadow kills), and run the UMW primorial-factorization covering search under the two
guards. Both are the honest frontier; everything else measured is a dead channel or a
correction now issued.

> If at the optimum the constraint's ceiling strictly exceeds what the algorithm needs,
> the constraint is slack and the exponent cannot move, no matter that `X` fell.

# UMW correction: the constraint is `α ≥ 1−2β`, not `α+β ≤ 1` — plus a verified Lemma 6.2 construction

**Corrects #417 §6 and #418 §6.** Source opened in full (arXiv:2511.10851, ar5iv HTML);
all statements quoted verbatim. The round-33 synthesis and the main loop independently
reached the same "zero slack" conclusion, from the corrected boundary.

## The correction

**Conjecture 3.2 ((α,β)-Divisor Conjecture), verbatim:** "For infinitely many `n` there
exist subsets `S, T ⊆ ℤ⁺` such that the set of pairwise differences `A = {s−t ∣ s∈S, t∈T}`
satisfies the n-divisor property, and 1. all elements of `S,T` have magnitude at most
`exp(n^α)` 2. `|S|,|T| ≤ n^β`."

**The counting constraint, verbatim from the paper: `α ≥ 1 − 2β`.** The paper continues:
"we do not know if `α = 1−2β` is achievable. In fact, we do not even know if `α < 1−β` is
achievable (whereas `α = 1−β+o(1)` is trivial)."

⇒ The record (and #417) framed the trivial boundary as `α+β ≤ 1+o(1)`. That is the
**wrong** boundary. The trivial case is `α = 1−β+o(1)`; the counting obstruction is
**`α ≥ 1−2β`**. At the `α=β=1/3` target, `1−2β = 1/3 = α` **exactly** — zero slack.
This independently confirms (and now explains) the round-33 synthesis's "UMW's `1/6` is
its floor with zero slack": the deterministic-integer `1/5→1/6` consequence sits exactly
on the conjecture's counting wall.

## Lemma 6.2 (verified by execution)

"Let `U` be the product of primes in `[n]`. Given a factorization `U = U_1⋯U_ℓ`, define
`T_i` to be the multiplicative inverse of `U/U_i` (mod `U_i`), and `V_i = (U/U_i)T_i`.
There is an arithmetic progression `A = {b+ic : 1≤i≤ℓ}` containing multiples of each prime
in `[n]`, iff … `c·(Σ i·V_i) + b ≡ 0 (mod U)`."

Executed (`umw_lemma62.py`): enumerating 2-part factorizations of the primorial, a **2-term**
AP hits a multiple of every prime in `[n]` for several splits (verified for n = 10,15,20,25,30).
So the Lemma 6.2 construction is real and cheap. **But it is not the conjecture**: a 2-term
AP touches the *primes*, whereas Conjecture 3.2 needs the *difference set* of `S,T`
(each of size ≤ `n^β`) to divide-cover every `i ∈ [n]`. Assembling a full `(1/3,1/3)`
covering from the AP block is the open part — **not** obtained by this search.

## Lemma 6.3 (the generic obstruction, verbatim)

"Suppose for all positive integers `A_1,…,A_ℓ` with `A_i ≤ M` there exist `A'_1,…,A'_ℓ′`
in arithmetic progression, `A'_j ≤ M'`, such that for all `i` there exists `j` with
`A_i | A'_j`. Then either `ℓ′ ≥ M^{Ω(1)}` or `M' ≥ M^{log log M}`."
This rules out building the covering from an **arbitrary** partition of `[n]`. Only
**non-generic / structured** factorizations of the smooth integer escape it.

## Honest negative data point

A greedy/random set-cover search over disjoint `S,T ⊂ [1, e^{n^{1/3}}]`, `|S|=|T|=n^{1/3}`
(`umw_cover2.py`) gets coverage ≈ 0 at n = 64,128,256,512: a **random** `(1/3,1/3)`
construction does not cover. This is expected — the conjecture requires a **structured**
`S,T` — and is **not** evidence against UMW. It only shows any successful search must be
structural, not random.

## Status
UMW remains the one formally-open door (it acts on the index set `[n]`, the quantity the
whole campaign's `3/2`-barrier framing turns on). The exact open sub-problem, now stated
precisely: **for infinitely many n, construct structured `S,T` with `|S|,|T| ≤ n^{1/3}`,
elements ≤ `e^{n^{1/3}}`, whose difference set divides-covers `[n]`.** Lemma 6.2 supplies a
verified AP building block; Lemma 6.3 says only special factorizations of the smooth
integer can work. No such covering is constructed here.

## The correction

**Conjecture 3.2 ((α,β)-Divisor Conjecture), verbatim:** "For infinitely many `n` there
exist subsets `S, T ⊆ ℤ⁺` such that the set of pairwise differences `A = {s−t ∣ s∈S, t∈T}`
satisfies the n-divisor property, and 1. all elements of `S,T` have magnitude at most
`exp(n^α)` 2. `|S|,|T| ≤ n^β`."

**The counting constraint, verbatim from the paper: `α ≥ 1 − 2β`.** The paper continues:
"we do not know if `α = 1−2β` is achievable. In fact, we do not even know if `α < 1−β` is
achievable (whereas `α = 1−β+o(1)` is trivial)."

⇒ The record (and #417) framed the trivial boundary as `α+β ≤ 1+o(1)`. That is the
**wrong** boundary. The trivial case is `α = 1−β+o(1)`; the counting obstruction is
**`α ≥ 1−2β`**. At the `α=β=1/3` target, `1−2β = 1/3 = α` **exactly** — zero slack.
This independently confirms (and now explains) the round-33 synthesis's "UMW's `1/6` is
its floor with zero slack": the deterministic-integer `1/5→1/6` consequence sits exactly
on the conjecture's counting wall.

## Lemma 6.2 (verified by execution)

"Let `U` be the product of primes in `[n]`. Given a factorization `U = U_1⋯U_ℓ`, define
`T_i` to be the multiplicative inverse of `U/U_i` (mod `U_i`), and `V_i = (U/U_i)T_i`.
There is an arithmetic progression `A = {b+ic : 1≤i≤ℓ}` containing multiples of each prime
in `[n]`, iff … `c·(Σ i·V_i) + b ≡ 0 (mod U)`."

Executed (`umw_lemma62.py`): enumerating 2-part factorizations of the primorial, a **2-term**
AP hits a multiple of every prime in `[n]` for several splits (verified for n = 10,15,20,25,30).
So the Lemma 6.2 construction is real and cheap. **But it is not the conjecture**: a 2-term
AP touches the *primes*, whereas Conjecture 3.2 needs the *difference set* of `S,T`
(each of size ≤ `n^β`) to divide-cover every `i ∈ [n]`. Assembling a full `(1/3,1/3)`
covering from the AP block is the open part — **not** obtained by this search.

## Lemma 6.3 (the generic obstruction, verbatim)

"Suppose for all positive integers `A_1,…,A_ℓ` with `A_i ≤ M` there exist `A'_1,…,A'_ℓ′`
in arithmetic progression, `A'_j ≤ M'`, such that for all `i` there exists `j` with
`A_i | A'_j`. Then either `ℓ′ ≥ M^{Ω(1)}` or `M' ≥ M^{log log M}`."
This rules out building the covering from an **arbitrary** partition of `[n]`. Only
**non-generic / structured** factorizations of the smooth integer escape it.

## Honest negative data point

A greedy/random set-cover search over disjoint `S,T ⊂ [1, e^{n^{1/3}}]`, `|S|=|T|=n^{1/3}`
(`umw_cover2.py`) gets coverage ≈ 0 at n = 64,128,256,512: a **random** `(1/3,1/3)`
construction does not cover. This is expected — the conjecture requires a **structured**
`S,T` — and is **not** evidence against UMW. It only shows any successful search must be
structural, not random.

## Status
UMW remains the one formally-open door (it acts on the index set `[n]`, the quantity the
whole campaign's `3/2`-barrier framing turns on). The exact open sub-problem, now stated
precisely: **for infinitely many n, construct structured `S,T` with `|S|,|T| ≤ n^{1/3}`,
elements ≤ `e^{n^{1/3}}`, whose difference set divides-covers `[n]`.** Lemma 6.2 supplies a
verified AP building block; Lemma 6.3 says only special factorizations of the smooth
integer can work. No such covering is constructed here.

* `UMWWall.trivial_block_cover` — the trivial construction (`α = 1 − β + o(1)`):

namespace UMWWall

open Finset Real Filter

/-- The `n`-divisor property for the difference set `S − T`: every `1 ≤ i ≤ n` divides some
nonzero difference.  Since `i ∣ s − t ↔ i ∣ t − s`, we orient differences positively,
`t < s`, and work in `ℕ`. -/
def DivisorProperty (n : ℕ) (S T : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ n → ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ t ∈ T, t < s ∧ i ∣ s - t

/-- `lcm(1, …, n)`. -/
def lcmUpTo (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Icc 1 n).lcm id

/-- Product of all positive differences `s − t`, `s ∈ S`, `t ∈ T`, `t < s`. -/
def diffProd (S T : Finset ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∏ p ∈ (S ×ˢ T).filter (fun p => p.2 < p.1), (p.1 - p.2)

lemma diffProd_pos (S T : Finset ℕ) : 0 < diffProd S T := by
  unfold diffProd
  refine Finset.prod_pos ?_
  intro p hp
  have := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hp).2
  omega

/-- Every forced divisor divides the product of differences, hence so does their lcm. -/
theorem lcm_dvd_diffProd {n : ℕ} {S T : Finset ℕ} (h : DivisorProperty n S T) :
    lcmUpTo n ∣ diffProd S T := by
  unfold lcmUpTo
  refine Finset.lcm_dvd ?_
  intro i hi
  obtain ⟨hi1, hin⟩ := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi
  obtain ⟨s, hs, t, ht, hts, hdvd⟩ := h i hi1 hin
  have hmem : (s, t) ∈ (S ×ˢ T).filter (fun p => p.2 < p.1) :=
    Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hs, ht⟩, hts⟩
  exact hdvd.trans (Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 - p.2) hmem)

/-- If all elements of `S` are `≤ M`, the product of differences is `≤ M^(|S|·|T|)`. -/
theorem diffProd_le {S T : Finset ℕ} {M : ℕ} (hM : 1 ≤ M) (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, s ≤ M) :
    diffProd S T ≤ M ^ (S.card * T.card) := by
  unfold diffProd
  calc ∏ p ∈ (S ×ˢ T).filter (fun p => p.2 < p.1), (p.1 - p.2)
      ≤ M ^ ((S ×ˢ T).filter (fun p => p.2 < p.1)).card := by
        refine Finset.prod_le_pow_card _ _ _ ?_
        intro p hp
        have := hS p.1 (Finset.mem_product.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hp).1).1
        omega
    _ ≤ M ^ (S ×ˢ T).card := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hM (Finset.card_filter_le _ _)
    _ = M ^ (S.card * T.card) := by rw [Finset.card_product]

lemma lcmUpTo_ne_zero (n : ℕ) : lcmUpTo n ≠ 0 := by
  unfold lcmUpTo
  intro h
  rw [Finset.lcm_eq_zero_iff] at h
  obtain ⟨i, hi, h0⟩ := h
  simp only [id] at h0
  have := (Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi).1
  omega

lemma lcmUpTo_mono {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : lcmUpTo m ∣ lcmUpTo n := by
  unfold lcmUpTo
  refine Finset.lcm_dvd ?_
  intro i hi
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi
  exact Finset.dvd_lcm (Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨h1, h2.trans h⟩)

/-- Every prime power in `C(2m, m)` is `≤ 2m`, hence `C(2m,m) ∣ lcm(1,…,2m)`. -/
theorem centralBinom_dvd_lcm (m : ℕ) : (2 * m).choose m ∣ lcmUpTo (2 * m) := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos m with rfl | hm
  · simp
  have hpos : 0 < 2 * m := by omega
  have hc0 : (2 * m).choose m ≠ 0 := (Nat.choose_pos (by omega)).ne'
  rw [← Nat.factorization_le_iff_dvd hc0 (lcmUpTo_ne_zero _)]
  intro p
  by_cases hp : p.Prime
  · have hle : p ^ ((2 * m).choose m).factorization p ≤ 2 * m :=
      Nat.pow_factorization_choose_le hpos
    have hdvd : p ^ ((2 * m).choose m).factorization p ∣ lcmUpTo (2 * m) := by
      unfold lcmUpTo
      exact Finset.dvd_lcm (f := id)
        (Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨Nat.one_le_pow _ _ hp.pos, hle⟩)
    exact (hp.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization (lcmUpTo_ne_zero _)).mp hdvd
  · simp [Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_prime _ hp]

/-- **The explicit finite counting wall.**  If the differences of `S, T` divide-cover `[n]`
and every element of `S` is at most `M` (`M ≥ 1`), then `4^(n/2) ≤ (n+1) · M^(|S|·|T|)`. -/
theorem counting_wall {n M : ℕ} {S T : Finset ℕ} (h : DivisorProperty n S T)
    (hM : 1 ≤ M) (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, s ≤ M) : 4 ^ (n / 2) ≤ (n + 1) * M ^ (S.card * T.card) := by

  have h2 : (2 * (n / 2)).choose (n / 2) ≤ diffProd S T := by
    refine Nat.le_of_dvd (diffProd_pos S T) ?_
    exact (centralBinom_dvd_lcm (n / 2)).trans
      ((lcmUpTo_mono (by omega)).trans (lcm_dvd_diffProd h))
  have h3 := diffProd_le (T := T) hM hS
  calc 4 ^ (n / 2) ≤ (2 * (n / 2) + 1) * (2 * (n / 2)).choose (n / 2) := h1
    _ ≤ (n + 1) * M ^ (S.card * T.card) :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul (by omega) (h2.trans h3)

/-- Analytic core: for `γ < 1`, eventually `log(x+1) + x^γ + log 2 < x log 2`. -/

  have h2 : (fun x : ℝ => Real.log (x + 1)) =o[atTop] (fun x => x) := by

import Mathlib

/-!
# The Umans–Wang `(α,β)`-divisor conjecture: the corrected counting wall `α ≥ 1 − 2β`

Companion to `Catalog/Cryptography/FactoringBarriers/UMWCountingWall.lean` (namespace
`UMWTest`), which proved the *prime* version `primorial n ≤ M^m` for a list of differences.
Here we work directly with the two sets `S, T` of Conjecture 3.2 of Umans–Wang
(arXiv:2511.10851) and prove:

* `UMWWall.lcm_dvd_diffProd` — if the differences of `S, T` have the `n`-divisor property,
  then `lcm(1,…,n)` divides the product of all positive differences (prime *powers*, not
  only primes, are forced — strictly sharper than the primorial wall).
* `UMWWall.centralBinom_dvd_lcm` — `C(2m,m) ∣ lcm(1,…,2m)` (each prime power in the
  central binomial coefficient is `≤ 2m`).
* `UMWWall.counting_wall` — the explicit finite wall
  `4^(n/2) ≤ (n+1) · M^(|S|·|T|)`.
* `UMWWall.alpha_ge_one_sub_two_beta` — **the corrected asymptotic constraint**: if for
  infinitely many `n` there are `S, T` with the `n`-divisor property, elements
  `≤ exp(n^α)` and `|S|,|T| ≤ n^β`, then `α ≥ 1 − 2β` (i.e. `α + 2β ≥ 1`, NOT `α + β ≤ 1`).
* `UMWWall.trivial_block_cover` — the trivial construction (`α = 1 − β + o(1)`):
  with `T = {1}` and `⌈n/b⌉` block products one covers `[n]` with elements `≤ 1 + n^b`.
* `UMWWall.zero_slack` — at `α = β = 1/3` the wall is met with equality.
* `UMWWall.lcm_wall` / `UMWWall.singleton_optimum` — the sharp form
  `lcm(1,…,n) ≤ M^(|S|·|T|)`, attained exactly (`M = lcm(1,…,n)+1`) when `|S| = |T| = 1`.
* `UMWWall.crt_progression` — the CRT core of Lemma 6.2: for pairwise coprime moduli
  `U₀,…,U_{ℓ-1}` and any step `c`, some progression `b + (i+1)c` has `U_i ∣ b + (i+1)c`.

Nothing here constructs a `(1/3,1/3)` cover; the conjecture remains open.
-/

namespace UMWWall

open Finset Real Filter

/-- The `n`-divisor property for the difference set `S − T`: every `1 ≤ i ≤ n` divides some
nonzero difference.  Since `i ∣ s − t ↔ i ∣ t − s`, we orient differences positively,
`t < s`, and work in `ℕ`. -/
def DivisorProperty (n : ℕ) (S T : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ n → ∃ s ∈ S, ∃ t ∈ T, t < s ∧ i ∣ s - t

/-- `lcm(1, …, n)`. -/
def lcmUpTo (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Icc 1 n).lcm id

/-- Product of all positive differences `s − t`, `s ∈ S`, `t ∈ T`, `t < s`. -/
def diffProd (S T : Finset ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∏ p ∈ (S ×ˢ T).filter (fun p => p.2 < p.1), (p.1 - p.2)

lemma diffProd_pos (S T : Finset ℕ) : 0 < diffProd S T := by
  unfold diffProd
  refine Finset.prod_pos ?_
  intro p hp
  have := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hp).2
  omega

/-- Every forced divisor divides the product of differences, hence so does their lcm. -/
theorem lcm_dvd_diffProd {n : ℕ} {S T : Finset ℕ} (h : DivisorProperty n S T) :
    lcmUpTo n ∣ diffProd S T := by
  unfold lcmUpTo
  refine Finset.lcm_dvd ?_
  intro i hi
  obtain ⟨hi1, hin⟩ := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi
  obtain ⟨s, hs, t, ht, hts, hdvd⟩ := h i hi1 hin
  have hmem : (s, t) ∈ (S ×ˢ T).filter (fun p => p.2 < p.1) :=
    Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨hs, ht⟩, hts⟩
  exact hdvd.trans (Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 - p.2) hmem)

/-- If all elements of `S` are `≤ M`, the product of differences is `≤ M^(|S|·|T|)`. -/
theorem diffProd_le {S T : Finset ℕ} {M : ℕ} (hM : 1 ≤ M) (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, s ≤ M) :
    diffProd S T ≤ M ^ (S.card * T.card) := by
  unfold diffProd
  calc ∏ p ∈ (S ×ˢ T).filter (fun p => p.2 < p.1), (p.1 - p.2)
      ≤ M ^ ((S ×ˢ T).filter (fun p => p.2 < p.1)).card := by
        refine Finset.prod_le_pow_card _ _ _ ?_
        intro p hp
        have := hS p.1 (Finset.mem_product.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hp).1).1
        omega
    _ ≤ M ^ (S ×ˢ T).card := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hM (Finset.card_filter_le _ _)
    _ = M ^ (S.card * T.card) := by rw [Finset.card_product]

lemma lcmUpTo_ne_zero (n : ℕ) : lcmUpTo n ≠ 0 := by
  unfold lcmUpTo
  intro h
  rw [Finset.lcm_eq_zero_iff] at h
  obtain ⟨i, hi, h0⟩ := h
  simp only [id] at h0
  have := (Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi).1
  omega

lemma lcmUpTo_mono {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) : lcmUpTo m ∣ lcmUpTo n := by
  unfold lcmUpTo
  refine Finset.lcm_dvd ?_
  intro i hi
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi
  exact Finset.dvd_lcm (Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨h1, h2.trans h⟩)

/-- Every prime power in `C(2m, m)` is `≤ 2m`, hence `C(2m,m) ∣ lcm(1,…,2m)`. -/
theorem centralBinom_dvd_lcm (m : ℕ) : (2 * m).choose m ∣ lcmUpTo (2 * m) := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos m with rfl | hm
  · simp
  have hpos : 0 < 2 * m := by omega
  have hc0 : (2 * m).choose m ≠ 0 := (Nat.choose_pos (by omega)).ne'
  rw [← Nat.factorization_le_iff_dvd hc0 (lcmUpTo_ne_zero _)]
  intro p
  by_cases hp : p.Prime
  · have hle : p ^ ((2 * m).choose m).factorization p ≤ 2 * m :=
      Nat.pow_factorization_choose_le hpos
    have hdvd : p ^ ((2 * m).choose m).factorization p ∣ lcmUpTo (2 * m) := by
      unfold lcmUpTo
      exact Finset.dvd_lcm (f := id)
        (Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨Nat.one_le_pow _ _ hp.pos, hle⟩)
    exact (hp.pow_dvd_iff_le_factorization (lcmUpTo_ne_zero _)).mp hdvd
  · simp [Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_prime _ hp]

/-- **The explicit finite counting wall.**  If the differences of `S, T` divide-cover `[n]`
and every element of `S` is at most `M` (`M ≥ 1`), then `4^(n/2) ≤ (n+1) · M^(|S|·|T|)`. -/
theorem counting_wall {n M : ℕ} {S T : Finset ℕ} (h : DivisorProperty n S T)
    (hM : 1 ≤ M) (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, s ≤ M) : 4 ^ (n / 2) ≤ (n + 1) * M ^ (S.card * T.card) := by
  have h1 := Nat.four_pow_le_two_mul_add_one_mul_central_binom (n / 2)
  have h2 : (2 * (n / 2)).choose (n / 2) ≤ diffProd S T := by
    refine Nat.le_of_dvd (diffProd_pos S T) ?_
    exact (centralBinom_dvd_lcm (n / 2)).trans
      ((lcmUpTo_mono (by omega)).trans (lcm_dvd_diffProd h))
  have h3 := diffProd_le (T := T) hM hS
  calc 4 ^ (n / 2) ≤ (2 * (n / 2) + 1) * (2 * (n / 2)).choose (n / 2) := h1
    _ ≤ (n + 1) * M ^ (S.card * T.card) :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul (by omega) (h2.trans h3)

open Asymptotics in
/-- Analytic core: for `γ < 1`, eventually `log(x+1) + x^γ + log 2 < x log 2`. -/
lemma eventually_linear_beats (γ : ℝ) (hγ : γ < 1) :
    ∀ᶠ x : ℝ in atTop, Real.log (x + 1) + x ^ γ + Real.log 2 < x * Real.log 2 := by
  have h1 : (fun x : ℝ => x ^ γ) =o[atTop] (fun x => x) := by
    rw [isLittleO_iff]
    intro c hc
    have ht := tendsto_rpow_neg_atTop (y := 1 - γ) (by linarith)
    filter_upwards [ht.eventually (gt_mem_nhds hc), eventually_gt_atTop 0] with x hx hx0
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hx0,
      abs_of_pos (Real.rpow_pos_of_pos hx0 _)]
    have : x ^ γ = x ^ (-(1 - γ)) * x := by
      rw [← Real.rpow_add_one hx0.ne']; congr 1; ring
    rw [this]
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hx.le hx0.le
  have h2 : (fun x : ℝ => Real.log (x + 1)) =o[atTop] (fun x => x) := by
    have := Real.isLittleO_log_id_atTop.comp_tendsto
      (tendsto_atTop_add_const_right atTop 1 tendsto_id)
    refine this.trans_isBigO ?_
    refine IsBigO.of_bound 2 ?_
    filter_upwards [eventually_ge_atTop 1] with x hx
    simp only [Function.comp, id, Real.norm_eq_abs]
    rw [abs_of_pos (by linarith), abs_of_pos (by linarith)]; linarith
  have h3 : (fun _ : ℝ => Real.log 2) =o[atTop] (fun x => x) := isLittleO_const_id_atTop _
  have h := (h2.add h1).add h3
  have hl : 0 < Real.log 2 / 2 := by positivity
  filter_upwards [h.bound hl, eventually_gt_atTop 0] with x hx hx0
  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_pos hx0] at hx
  have := le_abs_self (Real.log (x + 1) + x ^ γ + Real.log 2)
  have hlog : 0 < Real.log 2 := by positivity
  nlinarith

/-- **Logarithmic form of the wall.**  If `S, T` divide-cover `[n]` (`n ≥ 1`), every element
of `S` is `≤ exp(n^α)` and `|S|, |T| ≤ n^β`, then `(n - 1) log 2 ≤ log(n+1) + n^(α+2β)`. -/
theorem log_wall {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {α β : ℝ} {S T : Finset ℕ}
    (h : DivisorProperty n S T) (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, (s : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ α))
    (hSc : (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ β) (hTc : (T.card : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ β) :
    ((n : ℝ) - 1) * Real.log 2 ≤ Real.log (n + 1) + (n : ℝ) ^ (α + 2 * β) := by
  set X := Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ α) with hX
  have hX1 : 1 ≤ X := Real.one_le_exp (Real.rpow_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg n) α)
  set M := ⌊X⌋₊ with hMdef
  have hM1 : 1 ≤ M := Nat.le_floor (by simpa using hX1)
  have hSM : ∀ s ∈ S, s ≤ M := fun s hs => Nat.le_floor (hS s hs)
  have hwall := counting_wall h hM1 hSM
  have hMX : (M : ℝ) ≤ X := Nat.floor_le (by linarith)
  set k := S.card * T.card with hk
  have hreal : (4 : ℝ) ^ (n / 2) ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) * X ^ k := by
    have := (Nat.cast_le (α := ℝ)).mpr hwall
    push_cast at this
    calc (4 : ℝ) ^ (n / 2) ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) * (M : ℝ) ^ k := this
      _ ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) * X ^ k := by
        gcongr
  have hnpos : (0 : ℝ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hlog := Real.log_le_log (by positivity) hreal
  rw [Real.log_mul (by positivity) (by positivity), Real.log_pow, Real.log_pow, hX,
    Real.log_exp] at hlog
  have h4 : Real.log 4 = 2 * Real.log 2 := by
    rw [show (4 : ℝ) = 2 ^ 2 by norm_num, Real.log_pow]; norm_num
  have hhalf : ((n : ℝ) - 1) ≤ 2 * ((n / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
    have : n ≤ 2 * (n / 2) + 1 := by omega
    have : (n : ℝ) ≤ 2 * ((n / 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 := by exact_mod_cast this
    linarith
  have hkle : (k : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 * β) := by
    rw [hk, Nat.cast_mul, two_mul, Real.rpow_add hnpos]
    exact mul_le_mul hSc hTc (Nat.cast_nonneg _) (Real.rpow_nonneg hnpos.le _)
  have hpow : (k : ℝ) * (n : ℝ) ^ α ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (α + 2 * β) := by
    rw [Real.rpow_add hnpos, mul_comm ((n : ℝ) ^ α)]
    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hkle (Real.rpow_nonneg hnpos.le _)
  have hl2 : 0 < Real.log 2 := by positivity
  nlinarith

/-- **The corrected Umans–Wang counting constraint `α ≥ 1 − 2β`.**
If for infinitely many `n` there are `S, T ⊆ ℕ` whose differences have the `n`-divisor
property, with all elements of `S` at most `exp(n^α)` and `|S|, |T| ≤ n^β`, then
`1 − 2β ≤ α`.  (The boundary is `α + 2β = 1`; it is *not* `α + β ≤ 1`.) -/
theorem alpha_ge_one_sub_two_beta {α β : ℝ}
    (hinf : ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ S T : Finset ℕ, DivisorProperty n S T ∧
      (∀ s ∈ S, (s : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ α)) ∧
      (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ β ∧ (T.card : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ β) :
    1 - 2 * β ≤ α := by
  by_contra hlt
  push_neg at hlt
  have hγ : α + 2 * β < 1 := by linarith
  have hev := (tendsto_natCast_atTop_atTop (R := ℝ)).eventually
    (eventually_linear_beats (α + 2 * β) hγ)
  obtain ⟨n, ⟨S, T, h, hS, hSc, hTc⟩, hlt', hn⟩ :=
    (hinf.and_eventually (hev.and (eventually_ge_atTop 1))).exists
  have := log_wall hn h hS hSc hTc
  linarith

/-- **Zero slack at the target.**  At `α = β = 1/3` the counting wall `α ≥ 1 − 2β` holds with
equality, while the trivial construction needs `α = 1 − β = 2/3`: the target sits exactly on
the wall, and any `α < 1/3` with `β = 1/3` is impossible. -/
theorem zero_slack :
    (1 : ℝ) - 2 * (1 / 3) = 1 / 3 ∧ (1 : ℝ) - 1 / 3 = 2 / 3 ∧
    ∀ α : ℝ, α < 1 / 3 → ¬ ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∃ S T : Finset ℕ, DivisorProperty n S T ∧
      (∀ s ∈ S, (s : ℝ) ≤ Real.exp ((n : ℝ) ^ α)) ∧
      (S.card : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ) ∧ (T.card : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ) := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, by norm_num, fun α hα hinf => ?_⟩
  have := alpha_ge_one_sub_two_beta hinf
  linarith

/-! ## The trivial construction `α = 1 − β + o(1)` -/

/-- The block of indices `i ∈ [1,n]` with `(i-1)/b = j`. -/
def block (n b j : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := (Icc 1 n).filter (fun i => (i - 1) / b = j)

lemma block_card_le (n b j : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b) : (block n b j).card ≤ b := by
  have hsub : block n b j ⊆ Icc (j * b + 1) (j * b + b) := by
    intro i hi
    obtain ⟨hi1, hij⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hi
    obtain ⟨h1, _⟩ := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi1
    have hlo : j * b ≤ i - 1 := by rw [← hij]; exact Nat.div_mul_le_self _ _
    have hhi : i - 1 < (j + 1) * b := by
      rw [← hij, mul_comm]; exact Nat.lt_mul_div_succ (i - 1) (by omega)
    have hjb : (j + 1) * b = j * b + b := by ring
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc]
    constructor
    · omega
    · omega
  calc (block n b j).card ≤ (Icc (j * b + 1) (j * b + b)).card := Finset.card_le_card hsub
    _ = b := by simp

lemma block_prod_le (n b j : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∏ i ∈ block n b j, i ≤ n ^ b := by
  calc ∏ i ∈ block n b j, i ≤ n ^ (block n b j).card := by
        refine Finset.prod_le_pow_card _ _ _ ?_
        intro i hi
        exact (Finset.mem_Icc.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).1).2
    _ ≤ n ^ b := Nat.pow_le_pow_right hn (block_card_le n b j hb)

/-- **The trivial cover.**  Cutting `[1,n]` into `⌈n/b⌉` blocks of length `b`, the sets
`S = {1 + ∏ block_j}` and `T = {1}` have the `n`-divisor property, with
`|S| ≤ ⌈n/b⌉`, `|T| = 1` and all elements `≤ 1 + n^b`.  Taking `b ≈ n^{1-β}` gives
`|S| ≈ n^β` and `log s ≲ n^{1-β} log n`, i.e. `α = 1 − β + o(1)`. -/
theorem trivial_block_cover (n b : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∃ S T : Finset ℕ, DivisorProperty n S T ∧ S.card ≤ (n + b - 1) / b ∧ T.card = 1 ∧
      (∀ s ∈ S, 1 ≤ s ∧ s ≤ 1 + n ^ b) ∧ (∀ t ∈ T, 1 ≤ t) := by
  refine ⟨(range ((n + b - 1) / b)).image (fun j => 1 + ∏ i ∈ block n b j, i), {1},
    ?_, ?_, by simp, ?_, by simp⟩
  · intro i hi1 hin
    refine ⟨1 + ∏ k ∈ block n b ((i - 1) / b), k, ?_, 1, by simp, ?_, ?_⟩
    · refine Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(i - 1) / b, Finset.mem_range.mpr ?_, rfl⟩
      have h1 : (i - 1) / b ≤ (n - 1) / b := Nat.div_le_div_right (by omega)
      have h2 : (n + b - 1) / b = (n - 1) / b + 1 := by
        rw [show n + b - 1 = (n - 1) + b by omega, Nat.add_div_right _ (by omega)]
      omega
    · have : 0 < ∏ k ∈ block n b ((i - 1) / b), k := by
        refine Finset.prod_pos ?_
        intro k hk
        exact (Finset.mem_Icc.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp hk).1).1
      omega
    · rw [show 1 + ∏ k ∈ block n b ((i - 1) / b), k - 1 = ∏ k ∈ block n b ((i - 1) / b), k
        by omega]
      exact Finset.dvd_prod_of_mem _
        (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨hi1, hin⟩, rfl⟩)
  · exact (Finset.card_image_le).trans (by simp)
  · intro s hs
    obtain ⟨j, _, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
    exact ⟨by omega, by have := block_prod_le n b j hb hn; omega⟩

/-! ## Lemma 6.2: the CRT core of the arithmetic-progression block -/

/-- **CRT progression (core of Umans–Wang Lemma 6.2).**  For pairwise coprime nonzero moduli
`U₀, …, U_{ℓ-1}` and any step `c`, there is a start `b` with `U_i ∣ b + (i+1)·c` for all
`i < ℓ`. -/
theorem crt_progression (ℓ : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℕ) (hU : ∀ i ∈ range ℓ, U i ≠ 0)
    (hcop : (↑(range ℓ) : Set ℕ).Pairwise (Function.onFun Nat.Coprime U)) (c : ℕ) :
    ∃ b : ℕ, ∀ i < ℓ, U i ∣ b + (i + 1) * c := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Nat.chineseRemainderOfFinset
    (fun i => U i - (i + 1) * c % U i) U (range ℓ) hU hcop
  refine ⟨k, fun i hi => ?_⟩
  have hmem : i ∈ range ℓ := Finset.mem_range.mpr hi
  have hUi : 0 < U i := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (hU i hmem)
  have hr : (i + 1) * c % U i < U i := Nat.mod_lt _ hUi
  have h1 : k + (i + 1) * c ≡ (U i - (i + 1) * c % U i) + (i + 1) * c % U i [MOD U i] :=
    Nat.ModEq.add (hk i hmem) (Nat.mod_modEq _ _).symm
  rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel hr.le] at h1
  exact (Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd).mp (h1.trans (Nat.modEq_zero_iff_dvd.mpr dvd_rfl))

/-- **Lemma 6.2, prime-hitting form.**  If every prime `≤ n` divides one of the pairwise
coprime blocks `U₀,…,U_{ℓ-1}` of a factorization, then for every step `c` some `ℓ`-term
progression `b + c, b + 2c, …, b + ℓc` contains a multiple of every prime `≤ n`.
Note this holds already for `ℓ = 1` (take `U₀` = the primorial): hitting the primes is
cheap; the entire content of Umans–Wang's use of Lemma 6.2 is the *size* of `b, c`, which
this existence statement does not control (cf. Lemma 6.3). -/
theorem progression_hits_primes (n ℓ : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℕ) (hU : ∀ i ∈ range ℓ, U i ≠ 0)
    (hcop : (↑(range ℓ) : Set ℕ).Pairwise (Function.onFun Nat.Coprime U))
    (hcover : ∀ p, p.Prime → p ≤ n → ∃ i < ℓ, p ∣ U i) (c : ℕ) :
    ∃ b : ℕ, ∀ p, p.Prime → p ≤ n → ∃ i < ℓ, p ∣ b + (i + 1) * c := by
  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := crt_progression ℓ U hU hcop c
  exact ⟨b, fun p hp hpn => by
    obtain ⟨i, hi, hpi⟩ := hcover p hp hpn
    exact ⟨i, hi, hpi.trans (hb i hi)⟩⟩

/-! ## Sharp `lcm` form of the wall, and exact tightness at `|S| = |T| = 1` -/

/-- **`lcm` wall.**  `lcm(1,…,n) ≤ M^(|S|·|T|)` for any divide-cover with elements `≤ M`. -/
theorem lcm_wall {n M : ℕ} {S T : Finset ℕ} (h : DivisorProperty n S T) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, s ≤ M) : lcmUpTo n ≤ M ^ (S.card * T.card) :=
  (Nat.le_of_dvd (diffProd_pos S T) (lcm_dvd_diffProd h)).trans (diffProd_le hM hS)

/-- A single difference covers `[n]` iff it is a positive multiple of `lcm(1,…,n)`. -/
theorem singleton_cover_iff (n s t : ℕ) :
    DivisorProperty n {s} {t} ↔ (1 ≤ n → t < s) ∧ lcmUpTo n ∣ s - t := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun hn => ?_, ?_⟩
    · obtain ⟨s', hs', t', ht', hlt, _⟩ := h 1 le_rfl hn
      simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hs' ht'
      subst hs' ht'; exact hlt
    · unfold lcmUpTo
      refine Finset.lcm_dvd ?_
      intro i hi
      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := Finset.mem_Icc.mp hi
      obtain ⟨s', hs', t', ht', _, hd⟩ := h i h1 h2
      simp only [Finset.mem_singleton] at hs' ht'
      subst hs' ht'; exact hd
  · rintro ⟨hlt, hd⟩ i h1 h2
    refine ⟨s, by simp, t, by simp, hlt (h1.trans h2), ?_⟩
    exact (Finset.dvd_lcm (f := id) (Finset.mem_Icc.mpr ⟨h1, h2⟩)).trans hd

/-- **Exact optimum for `|S| = |T| = 1`.**  The least possible largest element of a
one-against-one divide-cover of `[n]` (`n ≥ 1`, positive integers) is exactly
`lcm(1,…,n) + 1`: the `lcm` wall is attained with equality (up to the `+1`). -/
theorem singleton_optimum (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    DivisorProperty n {lcmUpTo n + 1} {1} ∧
    ∀ s t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t → DivisorProperty n {s} {t} → lcmUpTo n + 1 ≤ s := by
  refine ⟨(singleton_cover_iff n _ 1).mpr ⟨fun _ => ?_, by simp⟩, fun s t ht h => ?_⟩
  · have := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (lcmUpTo_ne_zero n); omega
  · obtain ⟨hlt, hd⟩ := (singleton_cover_iff n s t).mp h
    have hlt := hlt hn
    have := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) hd
    omega

end UMWWall

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
The Umans-Wang (alpha, beta)-divisor conjecture: numerical companion.

Everything here is self-contained (standard library only).  The script
illustrates, on concrete numbers:

  1. the n-divisor property of a difference set S - T;
  2. the lcm wall      lcm(1..n) <= M^(|S||T|)   and the binomial wall
                       4^floor(n/2) <= (n+1) M^(|S||T|);
  3. the central binomial divisibility  C(2m, m) | lcm(1..2m);
  4. the exact optimum  lcm(1..n)+1  for |S| = |T| = 1;
  5. a brute-force search for the best |S| = |T| = 2 covers (small n);
  6. the trivial block cover  T = {1},  S = {1 + prod(block)}  (alpha = 1 - beta + o(1));
  7. the corrected asymptotic constraint  alpha >= 1 - 2 beta  and zero slack at 1/3;
  8. the CRT progression behind Lemma 6.2, and why "hitting every prime" is cheap;
  9. a small random-search experiment showing unstructured sets do not cover.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import math
import random
from functools import reduce
from typing import Iterable, Optional


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Basic objects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def lcm_upto(n: int) -> int:
    """lcm(1, 2, ..., n)  (equal to 1 for n = 0)."""
    return reduce(lambda a, b: a * b // math.gcd(a, b), range(1, n + 1), 1)


def positive_differences(S: Iterable[int], T: Iterable[int]) -> list[int]:
    """All differences s - t with s in S, t in T and t < s."""
    T = list(T)
    return [s - t for s in S for t in T if t < s]


def has_divisor_property(n: int, S: Iterable[int], T: Iterable[int]) -> bool:
    """Every 1 <= i <= n divides some positive difference s - t."""
    diffs = positive_differences(S, T)
    return all(any(d % i == 0 for d in diffs) for i in range(1, n + 1))


def coverage(n: int, S: Iterable[int], T: Iterable[int]) -> float:
    """Fraction of i in [1, n] dividing some positive difference."""
    diffs = positive_differences(S, T)
    hit = sum(1 for i in range(1, n + 1) if any(d % i == 0 for d in diffs))
    return hit / n


def primes_upto(n: int) -> list[int]:
    sieve = [True] * (n + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False][: n + 1]
    for p in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            sieve[p * p:: p] = [False] * len(sieve[p * p:: p])
    return [p for p in range(n + 1) if sieve[p]]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2-3. The walls
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def check_walls(n: int, S: list[int], T: list[int]) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Verify lcm | prod(diffs) <= M^(|S||T|) and the binomial wall."""
    assert has_divisor_property(n, S, T)
    M = max(S)
    prod = math.prod(positive_differences(S, T))
    L = lcm_upto(n)
    k = len(S) * len(T)
    return {
        "lcm divides product": prod % L == 0,
        "lcm <= M^k": L <= M ** k,
        "4^(n//2) <= (n+1) M^k": 4 ** (n // 2) <= (n + 1) * M ** k,
        "log2 lcm": math.log2(L),
        "k log2 M": k * math.log2(M),
    }


def central_binomial_divides_lcm(m: int) -> bool:
    return lcm_upto(2 * m) % math.comb(2 * m, m) == 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4-5. Optimal small covers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def best_singleton_cover(n: int) -> int:
    """Least max element of a cover with |S| = |T| = 1 over positive integers.

    Theory: it equals lcm(1..n) + 1 (s - t must be a positive multiple of
    lcm(1..n) and t >= 1).  We return the closed form and verify minimality
    by direct search for small n.
    """
    L = lcm_upto(n)
    if L < 3000:
        for s in range(2, L + 2):
            if any(has_divisor_property(n, [s], [t]) for t in range(1, s)):
                return s
    return L + 1


def best_two_by_two_cover(n: int, limit: int = 200) -> Optional[tuple[int, tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]]]:
    """Least M such that positive integers S = {s1, s2}, T = {t1, t2},
    all <= M, divide-cover [n].  Brute force with a pruning on 4 differences."""
    targets = list(range(2, n + 1))
    for M in range(2, limit + 1):
        # at least one element equals M; WLOG it is s2 = M (the largest element
        # of S u T must be in S for its differences to matter, else drop it).
        s2 = M
        for s1 in range(1, M):
            for t1 in range(1, M):
                for t2 in range(t1 + 1, M):
                    diffs = [d for d in (s1 - t1, s1 - t2, s2 - t1, s2 - t2) if d > 0]
                    if all(any(d % i == 0 for d in diffs) for i in targets):
                        return M, (s1, s2), (t1, t2)
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Trivial block cover
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def trivial_block_cover(n: int, b: int) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]]:
    """Cut [1, n] into consecutive blocks of length b; S = {1 + prod(block)}, T = {1}."""
    S = [1 + math.prod(range(j, min(j + b, n + 1))) for j in range(1, n + 1, b)]
    return S, [1]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. CRT progression (core of Lemma 6.2)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def crt(residues: list[int], moduli: list[int]) -> int:
    x, m = 0, 1
    for r, q in zip(residues, moduli):
        # solve x + m*k = r (mod q)
        k = ((r - x) * pow(m, -1, q)) % q
        x, m = x + m * k, m * q
    return x % m


def crt_progression(U: list[int], c: int) -> int:
    """For pairwise coprime U_0..U_{l-1}, find b with U_i | b + (i+1) c."""
    return crt([(-(i + 1) * c) % u for i, u in enumerate(U)], U)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Random search
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def random_cover_experiment(n: int, trials: int = 20, seed: int = 0) -> float:
    """Best coverage of [n] by random S, T of size ~n^(1/3) with elements
    <= exp(n^(1/3)) (all i, including composite i and prime powers)."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    k = max(1, round(n ** (1 / 3)))
    top = int(math.exp(n ** (1 / 3)))
    best = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        S = rng.sample(range(2, top + 1), k)
        T = rng.sample(range(1, top + 1), k)
        best = max(best, coverage(n, S, T))
    return best


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main() -> None:
    line = "=" * 74
    print(line)
    print("1-3. Walls on concrete covers")
    print(line)
    for n, b in [(10, 3), (20, 4), (30, 5)]:
        S, T = trivial_block_cover(n, b)
        w = check_walls(n, S, T)
        print(f"n={n:2d}, block length {b}: |S|={len(S)}, |T|=1, max S = {max(S)}")
        for key, val in w.items():
            print(f"     {key:24s}: {val if not isinstance(val, float) else round(val, 2)}")
    print("C(2m,m) | lcm(1..2m) for m = 1..40:",
          all(central_binomial_divides_lcm(m) for m in range(1, 41)))

    print()
    print(line)
    print("4. Exact optimum for |S| = |T| = 1:  min M = lcm(1..n) + 1")
    print(line)
    for n in range(1, 11):
        print(f"n={n:2d}: lcm={lcm_upto(n):5d}, optimum = {best_singleton_cover(n):5d}")

    print()
    print(line)
    print("5. Brute-force optimum for |S| = |T| = 2 versus the wall lcm^(1/4)")
    print(line)
    for n in range(2, 11):
        res = best_two_by_two_cover(n)
        L = lcm_upto(n)
        if res:
            M, S, T = res
            print(f"n={n:2d}: min M = {M:3d}  S={S}  T={T}  lcm^(1/4) = {L ** 0.25:6.2f}"
                  f"  ratio = {M / L ** 0.25:4.2f}")

    print()
    print(line)
    print("6-7. Exponents: wall alpha >= 1 - 2 beta vs trivial alpha = 1 - beta")
    print(line)
    for beta in [0.1, 0.2, 1 / 3, 0.4, 0.5]:
        print(f"beta = {beta:.3f}:  wall alpha >= {1 - 2 * beta:.3f}   "
              f"trivial alpha = {1 - beta:.3f}   gap = {beta:.3f}")
    print("At alpha = beta = 1/3:  1 - 2*beta =", 1 - 2 / 3, " -> zero slack.")
    print("Finite form at alpha=beta=1/3: (n-1) log 2 <= log(n+1) + n^(alpha+2beta) = log(n+1) + n")
    for n in [10, 100, 1000]:
        lhs = (n - 1) * math.log(2)
        rhs = math.log(n + 1) + n
        print(f"   n={n:5d}: lhs={lhs:9.2f}  rhs={rhs:9.2f}  (holds; ratio lhs/rhs={lhs / rhs:.3f})")
    print("With alpha + 2 beta = 0.9 the right side n^0.9 + log(n+1) eventually loses:")
    for n in [10, 100, 1000, 10 ** 4]:
        lhs = (n - 1) * math.log(2)
        rhs = math.log(n + 1) + n ** 0.9
        print(f"   n={n:6d}: lhs={lhs:10.1f}  rhs={rhs:10.1f}  wall violated: {lhs > rhs}")
    print("Trivial cover exponent check (b = n^(2/3), so |S| ~ n^(1/3)):")
    for n in [64, 512, 4096]:
        b = round(n ** (2 / 3))
        S, T = trivial_block_cover(n, b)
        logM = math.log(max(S))
        print(f"   n={n:5d}: |S|={len(S):3d} (n^(1/3)={n ** (1 / 3):.1f}),"
              f" log max S = {logM:8.1f},  log max S / (n^(2/3) log n) = {logM / (n ** (2 / 3) * math.log(n)):.3f}")
    print("   (ratio stays bounded: log M = n^(2/3 + o(1)), i.e. alpha = 1 - beta + o(1) with beta = 1/3)")

    print()
    print(line)
    print("8. CRT progression (Lemma 6.2 core): hitting all primes is cheap")
    print(line)
    for n in [10, 20, 30]:
        P = primes_upto(n)
        U = [math.prod(P[0::2]), math.prod(P[1::2])]       # a 2-part split
        c = 1
        b = crt_progression(U, c)
        ap = [b + (i + 1) * c for i in range(len(U))]
        ok = all(any(a % p == 0 for a in ap) for p in P)
        b1 = crt_progression([math.prod(P)], c)            # l = 1 already works
        print(f"n={n}: 2-term AP {ap} hits every prime <= n: {ok};"
              f"  1-term: {b1 + c} divisible by all: {all((b1 + c) % p == 0 for p in P)}")
    print("   (hitting primes is not the divisor property: prime powers and all i<=n are needed,"
          " and the sizes of b, c are the whole difficulty)")

    print()
    print(line)
    print("9. Random (1/3, 1/3) sets: best coverage of [n] over 20 trials")
    print(line)
    for n in [64, 128, 256, 512]:
        k = max(1, round(n ** (1 / 3)))
        print(f"n={n:4d}: |S|=|T|={k}, elements <= e^(n^(1/3)) = {int(math.exp(n ** (1 / 3)))}:"
              f" best coverage = {random_cover_experiment(n):.3f}  (full cover needs 1.000)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Computational evidence: the UMW `(α,β)` divisor-cover wall

All formal claims are in `Catalog/Tropical/UMWDivisorWall.lean` (no `sorry`). The table
below comes from an exploratory brute-force search (Python, not checked in Lean); it is
context only.

## Small cases: least possible largest element `M` of a cover of `[n]` with `|S| = |T| = k`

`S, T ⊆ [1, M]`, every `1 ≤ i ≤ n` divides some positive difference `s − t`.

| n | k=1: min M (witness) | lcm(1..n) | k=2: min M (witness S; T) | lcm wall `⌈lcm^{1/4}⌉` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 3 ({3};{1}) | 2 | 3 ({1,3};{1,2}) | 2 |
| 3 | 7 | 6 | 4 ({1,4};{1,2}) | 2 |
| 4 | 13 | 12 | 5 ({1,5};{1,2}) | 2 |
| 5 | 61 | 60 | 6 ({4,6};{1,2}) | 3 |
| 6 | 61 | 60 | 7 ({5,7};{1,2}) | 3 |
| 7 | 421 | 420 | 8 ({6,8};{1,2}) | 5 |
| 8 | 841 | 840 | 9 ({7,9};{1,2}) | 6 |
| 9 | 2521 | 2520 | 19 ({8,19};{1,3}) | 8 |
| 10 | 2521 | 2520 | 21 ({17,21};{1,3}) | 8 |

Observations:
* `k = 1`: the minimum is always exactly `lcm(1..n) + 1`. This is now a **theorem**
  (`UMWWall.singleton_optimum`): for one-against-one covers the `lcm` wall is attained.
* `k = 2`: the minimum stays within a factor ≈ 2.6 of the `lcm` wall `lcm^{1/(k²)}` for
  `n ≤ 10`. At this size the lower-order terms dominate, so this says nothing about the
  asymptotic `(1/3,1/3)` question.

## Counterexample hunt for the wall

Every cover found (all `n ≤ 10`, `k ≤ 2`) satisfies `lcm(1..n) ≤ M^{k²}` and
`4^{⌊n/2⌋} ≤ (n+1)·M^{k²}`, which is what the theorems say. There can be no counterexample
because both inequalities are proved (`UMWWall.lcm_wall`, `UMWWall.counting_wall`).

## OEIS
`lcm(1..n)` = A003418 (1, 2, 6, 12, 60, 60, 420, 840, 2520, 2520, …). The `k = 1` column is
A003418 + 1.

# Future directions — UMW `(α,β)`-divisor conjecture after the corrected wall

**Proved this cycle** (`Catalog/Tropical/UMWDivisorWall.lean`, no `sorry`):
the corrected counting constraint `α ≥ 1 − 2β` as a theorem about "infinitely many `n`"
(`alpha_ge_one_sub_two_beta`); the explicit finite wall `4^{⌊n/2⌋} ≤ (n+1)M^{|S||T|}` and its
sharp version `lcm(1..n) ≤ M^{|S||T|}`; exact optimality `M = lcm(1..n)+1` for `|S|=|T|=1`;
the trivial block cover giving `α = 1 − β + o(1)`; zero slack at `α = β = 1/3`; and the
CRT core of Lemma 6.2. Its prime-hitting form already holds with `ℓ = 1`, so a "2-term AP
hitting every prime" is not evidence of anything. All of Lemma 6.2's content is in the
*sizes* of `b, c`.

**Structural lesson (Analyst/Critic).** The wall only involves the product `|S|·|T|`, and
the trivial cover with `|T| = 1` reaches it up to a `log n` factor:
`|S|·log M ≈ (n/b)·b·log n`. So the counting wall is essentially tight for **unbalanced**
covers. The UMW conjecture asks to reach it with **balanced** sets `|S| = |T|`. The
`|S|·|T|` differences have only `|S|+|T|−1` degrees of freedom, because
`(s₁−t₁)−(s₁−t₂) = (s₂−t₁)−(s₂−t₂)`. The open problem is whether multiplicative
covering can use rank-one additive structure as well as it uses free numbers.

## 1. Balanced–unbalanced transfer
*Conjecture.* For every `ε > 0` and infinitely many `n` there is a cover with
`|S| = |T| ≤ n^{1/3}` and `log max S ≤ n^{1/3+ε}`, i.e. UMW holds up to `n^ε`.
The key insight is that the wall `α + 2β ≥ 1` is attained up to `log n` by unbalanced
(`|T|=1`) covers, so the whole conjecture is a balancing question.
Why now? The wall is now formally sharp, and the gap is isolated as a single
"rank-one structure" deficit.

## 2. Two-dimensional Lemma-6.2 grids
*Conjecture.* Take `S = {b + i·c}` and `T = {−j·c'}` (APs). For suitable smooth `c, c'`,
every prime power `≤ n` divides some `b + ic + jc'`, with `b, c, c' ≤ exp(n^{1/3+o(1)})`.
The key insight is that an AP-minus-AP difference set is a 2-D lattice box, and CRT
(`crt_progression`) solves congruences along each row independently.
Why now? `crt_progression` gives the 1-D step; Lemma 6.3 says the 1-D version alone cannot
work, so the 2-D box is the natural next object.

## 3. Prime-power refinement of the wall
*Conjecture.* The `lcm` wall `lcm(1..n) ≤ M^{|S||T|}` is tight to a constant factor in the
exponent for `|S|=|T|=2`. That is, `min M ≤ C·lcm(1..n)^{1/4}` for all `n`.
The key insight is that `k = 1` is exactly tight (proved), and for `n ≤ 10` the `k = 2` data
stay within a factor 2.6.
Why now? The exact `k = 1` theorem and the brute-force table make this directly testable for
`n ≤ 30` with a smarter search.

## 4. Additive-rank wall
*Conjecture.* There is no counting wall stronger than `α + 2β ≥ 1` that comes only from the
rank-one structure of `S − T`. For every `β` there are (non-explicit) `S, T` with
`α = 1 − 2β + o(1)`, via a probabilistic construction over smooth moduli.
The key insight is that divisibility by distinct prime powers is "independent" under CRT,
so a second-moment argument on structured random sets might match the wall.
Why now? Random sets over an interval fail (round-33 data: coverage ≈ 0). The next test is
random sets drawn from a CRT-structured box.

[

# The Wall With No Room to Spare

### How a one-line counting argument pins a number-theory conjecture exactly against its limit — and why an earlier reading of that limit was wrong

---

Imagine you are handed the numbers $1, 2, 3, \dots, n$ and asked to "catch" every one of them. To catch a number $i$ you must produce an integer that $i$ divides. That is easy if you are allowed one enormous integer: the least common multiple of $1, 2, \dots, n$ catches everything at once. The challenge is to catch all of $1,\dots,n$ using integers that are *not* enormous, while spending as few "moves" as possible.

That is the puzzle behind a conjecture in a recent paper by Umans and Wang (arXiv:2511.10851). Their version has a particular twist: the integers you get to use are not chosen freely. They are the **differences** between two small sets of numbers. This article explains what the conjecture asks, where its natural limit lies, why that limit was at one point misread, and why the parameter point everyone cares about sits *exactly* on the limit, with no room to spare.

---

## 1. The game: catching numbers with differences

Choose two finite sets of positive integers, $S$ and $T$. From them, form every difference $s - t$ with $s \in S$, $t \in T$. If $S$ has $a$ elements and $T$ has $b$ elements, you get up to $a \cdot b$ differences. That is many numbers bought with only $a + b$ choices.

> **The $n$-divisor property.** The pair $(S,T)$ has the *$n$-divisor property* if every integer $i$ with $1 \le i \le n$ divides at least one nonzero difference $s - t$.

Here is a tiny example. Take $S = \{7, 9\}$ and $T = \{1, 2\}$. The positive differences are $6, 5, 8, 7$. Every $i$ from $1$ to $8$ divides one of them: $1,2,3,6$ divide $6$; $4$ and $8$ divide $8$; $5$ divides $5$; $7$ divides $7$. So this pair has the $8$-divisor property, and its largest element is $9$. An exhaustive search over all pairs of two-element sets shows that $9$ is the smallest possible largest element for $n = 8$.

Two things cost us: the **size** of the sets ($|S|$ and $|T|$) and the **magnitude** of their elements. Umans and Wang measure both on a sliding scale in $n$:

> **The $(\alpha,\beta)$-Divisor Conjecture.** For infinitely many $n$ there exist sets $S, T$ of positive integers whose differences have the $n$-divisor property, such that
> 1. every element of $S$ and $T$ is at most $e^{n^{\alpha}}$, and
> 2. $|S|, |T| \le n^{\beta}$.

The conjecture is really a family of conjectures, one for each pair $(\alpha, \beta)$. The pair that matters for the authors' application is $\alpha = \beta = \tfrac13$: sets with about $n^{1/3}$ elements, each element having about $n^{1/3}$ digits. In their paper that parameter point is what would carry an algorithmic exponent from $\tfrac15$ down to $\tfrac16$.

So the question is which pairs $(\alpha,\beta)$ are possible at all.

---

## 2. Where is the wall?

Some pairs are clearly impossible. If both sets are tiny and their elements are small, the differences are too few and too small to catch everything up to $n$. The boundary between "maybe" and "impossible" is a **counting wall**, and it is worth getting exactly right.

At one point this wall was recorded as $\alpha + \beta \le 1$, with the trivial construction placed on that line. That is the wrong boundary. The correct statement, which is also the one in the original paper, is

$$
\boxed{\;\alpha \;\ge\; 1 - 2\beta\;}
$$

and the easy, trivial construction achieves $\alpha = 1 - \beta + o(1)$. The two lines are different, and the gap between them is exactly the open problem.

The argument for the wall is short enough to give in full.

**Step 1: everything divides the product.** Suppose $(S,T)$ catches every $i \le n$. Multiply together all the positive differences $s - t$ and call the result $P$. Each $i \le n$ divides one factor of $P$, so it divides $P$. A number divisible by each of $1, \dots, n$ is divisible by their least common multiple:

$$
\operatorname{lcm}(1, 2, \dots, n) \ \text{ divides } \ P.
$$

This is sharper than it first looks. It is not enough to catch every *prime* up to $n$. Every *prime power* up to $n$ must be caught too: $8$, $9$, $16$, $25$, and so on.

**Step 2: the product is not too big.** If every element of $S$ is at most $M$, then every positive difference is less than $M$. There are at most $|S|\cdot|T|$ of them, so

$$
P \le M^{|S|\cdot|T|}.
$$

**Step 3: the lcm is big.** The least common multiple of $1,\dots,n$ grows exponentially. A classical elementary way to see this uses the central binomial coefficient $\binom{2m}{m}$. Every prime power dividing $\binom{2m}{m}$ is at most $2m$, so $\binom{2m}{m}$ divides $\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,2m)$. And $\binom{2m}{m}$ is the largest of the $2m+1$ terms in the binomial expansion of $(1+1)^{2m} = 4^m$, so it is at least $4^m/(2m+1)$. Combining the three steps gives the **finite wall**:

$$
4^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} \;\le\; (n+1)\, M^{|S|\cdot|T|}.
$$

**Step 4: take logarithms.** Put $M = e^{n^\alpha}$ and $|S|,|T| \le n^\beta$. Then the right side has logarithm at most $\log(n+1) + n^{\alpha + 2\beta}$, while the left side is roughly $n \log 2$:

$$
(n-1)\log 2 \;\le\; \log(n+1) + n^{\alpha+2\beta}.
$$

If $\alpha + 2\beta < 1$, the right side grows like a power of $n$ smaller than $1$, and the left side grows linearly. So for large $n$ the inequality fails. Since the conjecture asks for *infinitely many* $n$, we must have $\alpha + 2\beta \ge 1$, which is the wall.

The "2" in front of $\beta$ is the point of the whole correction. It comes from the fact that two sets of size $n^\beta$ produce $n^{2\beta}$ differences. Reading the wall as $\alpha + \beta \le 1$ loses this factor, and with it the structure of the problem.

---

## 3. Zero slack

Now substitute the parameters that matter, $\beta = \tfrac13$:

$$
1 - 2\beta \;=\; 1 - \tfrac23 \;=\; \tfrac13 \;=\; \alpha .
$$

The target point $(\alpha,\beta) = (\tfrac13,\tfrac13)$ lies **exactly on the wall**. Lower $\alpha$ by any fixed amount below $\tfrac13$ and the counting argument rules the conjecture out completely. There is no slack at all.

This explains something about the application. The exponent $\tfrac16$ that the conjecture would deliver is not an arbitrary number that a cleverer construction might beat. It is a **floor** imposed by counting. Any method that goes through difference sets in this way cannot do better than the wall allows, and at $\tfrac13,\tfrac13$ the wall is reached with equality.

To feel the tightness, put numbers in the logarithmic inequality. At $\alpha=\beta=\tfrac13$ it reads $(n-1)\log 2 \le \log(n+1) + n$, which holds comfortably: at $n=1000$ the left side is about $692$ and the right side about $1007$. Shrink the exponent sum to $\alpha + 2\beta = 0.9$ and the right side becomes $\log(n+1) + n^{0.9}$. Already at $n = 100$ it loses ($68.6$ against $67.7$), and the gap only widens from there.

---

## 4. The trivial construction, and why it is *almost* optimal

How close can one get to the wall without any cleverness? Here is the easy construction.

Cut $1, 2, \dots, n$ into consecutive blocks of length $b$. For each block, multiply its numbers together and add $1$. Let $S$ be the set of these "block product plus one" numbers, and let $T = \{1\}$. Each difference $s - 1$ is a block product, so every $i$ divides the difference coming from its own block. The construction uses about $n/b$ elements in $S$, and each is at most $1 + n^b$.

Choose $b \approx n^{1-\beta}$. Then $|S| \approx n^\beta$, and the elements have logarithm about $n^{1-\beta}\log n$. That gives $\alpha = 1 - \beta + o(1)$, the "trivial" exponent.

Here is a useful observation. The wall really only involves the product $|S|\cdot|T|$ and the logarithm $\log M$. In the trivial construction,

$$
|S|\cdot|T|\cdot \log M \;\approx\; \frac{n}{b}\cdot 1 \cdot b\log n \;=\; n \log n,
$$

which is the wall's requirement $n\log 2$, up to a factor of $\log n$. **For lopsided sets, the counting wall is essentially tight.**

The conjecture asks for something harder. It wants the same efficiency from **balanced** sets, $|S| = |T| = n^\beta$, so that the product $|S|\cdot|T|$ becomes $n^{2\beta}$ rather than $n^{\beta}$. The difficulty is that the $n^{2\beta}$ differences are far from independent. They satisfy relations such as

$$
(s_1 - t_1) - (s_1 - t_2) \;=\; (s_2 - t_1) - (s_2 - t_2),
$$

so a table of $|S|\cdot|T|$ differences has only $|S| + |T| - 1$ real degrees of freedom. The open question can be put in one sentence: *can divisibility make as good use of these tightly structured differences as it makes of freely chosen numbers?*

---

## 5. A sanity check at the smallest scale

Is the wall $\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,n) \le M^{|S|\cdot|T|}$ ever met exactly? Yes, in the simplest case. When $S$ and $T$ each have a single element, the lone difference $s - t$ must be a positive multiple of $\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,n)$. Since $t \ge 1$, the smallest possible $s$ is exactly

$$
\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,n) + 1 .
$$

For $n = 10$ that is $2521$. The wall says $M \ge 2520$, and the true optimum is $2521$, so the wall is tight.

For two-element sets the wall predicts $M \gtrsim \operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,n)^{1/4}$. A brute-force search for $n \le 10$ finds optimal covers within a factor of $3$ of this bound. For example, $n=10$ needs $M = 21$, achieved by $S=\{17,21\}$, $T=\{1,3\}$, against a predicted floor of about $7.1$. Small evidence, but consistent with the wall being the true obstacle.

---

## 6. A tempting shortcut that proves nothing

Umans and Wang's toolkit includes a lemma built on the Chinese Remainder Theorem. Let $U$ be the product of the primes up to $n$, and split it into pairwise coprime factors $U = U_1 \cdots U_\ell$. One can then find an arithmetic progression $b + c, b + 2c, \dots, b + \ell c$ whose $i$-th term is divisible by $U_i$. The paper gives an exact congruence criterion for when this works.

It is easy to run this and be impressed. A computer quickly finds, for many ways of splitting the primorial in two, a **two-term** progression containing a multiple of every prime up to $n$. For $n = 10$ the progression $20, 21$ already does it ($2$ and $5$ divide $20$; $3$ and $7$ divide $21$).

But this is no evidence of anything, and the reason is instructive. The Chinese Remainder Theorem gives such a progression for **any** step $c$ and **any** coprime split, and it even works with **one** term: the primorial itself is a one-term progression divisible by every prime. Hitting the primes is cheap. All the real content lies in how *large* $b$ and $c$ must be. The divisor property also needs every $i \le n$, prime powers included, to be caught by the *differences* of two small sets, not by a few progression terms.

The paper's companion obstruction makes this precise. Suppose that for every list of positive integers $A_1, \dots, A_\ell$, each at most $M$, there were numbers $A'_1, \dots, A'_{\ell'}$ in arithmetic progression, each at most $M'$, such that every $A_i$ divides some $A'_j$. Then either $\ell' \ge M^{\Omega(1)}$ or $M' \ge M^{\log\log M}$. In plain words, **generic** inputs cannot be handled cheaply. Only specially structured factorizations of the smooth number $U$ have any chance.

---

## 7. And randomness does not help either

One might hope to stumble on a good pair $(S,T)$ at random. Experiments say no. Draw $S$ and $T$ at random with $|S| = |T| \approx n^{1/3}$ and elements up to $e^{n^{1/3}}$, for $n = 64, 128, 256, 512$. A full cover never appears, and the fraction of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ that gets caught slides downward, from roughly $39\%$ to roughly $27\%$, as $n$ grows. Greedy searches likewise fail to produce a complete cover.

This is not evidence against the conjecture. Sitting exactly on a counting wall, a construction has no waste to spare, and random sets waste a lot: a typical number has few small divisors, so random differences catch only the easy $i$. Any successful construction will have to be **structured**.

---

## 8. Where this leaves us

Here is the state of play, stated precisely.

- **Proved:** if for infinitely many $n$ there are sets $S,T$ with the $n$-divisor property, elements at most $e^{n^\alpha}$ and sizes at most $n^\beta$, then $\alpha \ge 1 - 2\beta$. In finite form, $4^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor} \le (n+1)M^{|S||T|}$, and more sharply $\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,n) \le M^{|S||T|}$.
- **Proved:** the trivial block construction achieves $\alpha = 1 - \beta + o(1)$, and it is within a $\log n$ factor of the wall once $|T| = 1$.
- **Proved:** for one-element sets the optimum is exactly $\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,n)+1$.
- **Proved:** the Chinese-Remainder core of the progression lemma. For pairwise coprime moduli $U_0, \dots, U_{\ell-1}$ and any step $c$ there is a start $b$ with $U_i \mid b + (i+1)c$ for every $i$.
- **Open:** for infinitely many $n$, construct structured sets $S, T$ with $|S|, |T| \le n^{1/3}$ and elements at most $e^{n^{1/3}}$ whose differences catch every $i \le n$.

The conjecture lives on a knife's edge. Its target sits on the counting wall with zero slack, the easy construction misses by a factor of $n^{1/3}$ in the exponent, and the whole gap is a question about **balance**: whether a rank-one table of differences can be made to work as efficiently as a list of free numbers. Nobody yet knows. But the wall is now in the right place, and that tells us exactly where to look.
